cards.title: The English Tense System
rule: The English Tense System: Present & Past

Definition: The English Tense System (ናይ እንግሊዘኛ እዋን ስርዓት) is the grammatical system used to place an action or state in time (present or past) and describe its aspect—whether the action is a simple fact ($$\text{Simple Aspect}$$) or an ongoing, progressive process ($$\text{Progressive Aspect}$$).

In English, tenses do not merely express *when* an action occurs (present vs. past) but also *how* it occurs—its aspect (simple vs. progressive/continuous). Present Simple ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_{\text{1/s/es}}$$) and Present Continuous ($$\text{S} + \text{am/is/are} + \text{V-ing}$$) represent two distinct aspects of the present tense. Present Simple is used for habitual actions, general truths, and permanent states. Present Continuous is used for temporary actions happening at the exact moment of speaking. Tigrinya speakers often confuse these aspects because the boundaries between habitual actions and continuous actions are morphologically marked differently in Tigrinya. For example, the Tigrinya verb form "ይሰርሕ" can mean both "he works" (habitual) and "he is working" (continuous) depending on the helper verb "ኣሎ". This lack of a sharp morphological boundary often leads students to write "I am playing football every Saturday" instead of the correct simple present form.

examples.text: She goes to school every day.
She go to school every day.
examples.fix: She goes to school every day.

cards.title: Notes
body: The English Tense System: Present & Past

Definition: The English Tense System (ናይ እንግሊዘኛ እዋን ስርዓት) is the grammatical system used to place an action or state in time (present or past) and describe its aspect—whether the action is a simple fact ($$\text{Simple Aspect}$$) or an ongoing, progressive process ($$\text{Progressive Aspect}$$).

In English, tenses do not merely express *when* an action occurs (present vs. past) but also *how* it occurs—its aspect (simple vs. progressive/continuous). Present Simple ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_{\text{1/s/es}}$$) and Present Continuous ($$\text{S} + \text{am/is/are} + \text{V-ing}$$) represent two distinct aspects of the present tense. Present Simple is used for habitual actions, general truths, and permanent states. Present Continuous is used for temporary actions happening at the exact moment of speaking. Tigrinya speakers often confuse these aspects because the boundaries between habitual actions and continuous actions are morphologically marked differently in Tigrinya. For example, the Tigrinya verb form "ይሰርሕ" can mean both "he works" (habitual) and "he is working" (continuous) depending on the helper verb "ኣሎ". This lack of a sharp morphological boundary often leads students to write "I am playing football every Saturday" instead of the correct simple present form.

A critical area of difficulty for Tigrinya speakers is the use of Stative Verbs (ግሶች ናይ ስሚዒት ወይ ኩነታት - e.g., *know, understand, believe, want, love, seem, belong*). These verbs represent states rather than active physical processes and cannot be used in the progressive aspect ($$\times \text{I am knowing the answer}$$). Tigrinya frequently expresses states using continuous aspects (e.g., "ይርድኣኒ ኣሎ" - literally "It is understanding to me"), creating a strong L1 transfer error where students write "I am understanding the lesson" instead of "I understand the lesson." In ESSLCE exams, distractors will often present stative verbs in progressive forms to trap unwary students.

cards.title: Present perfect or past simple?
cards.problem: Complete: "I ____ (live) in Keren since 2018. Before that I ____ (live) in Mendefera for six years."

steps.text: **Step 1: Look at the time expressions.** "since 2018" links the past to now; "before that … for six years" is a finished period.
**Step 2: Unfinished period up to now → present perfect.** I have lived in Keren since 2018.
**Step 3: Finished period → past simple.** I lived in Mendefera for six years.
**Tip:** since/for + up to now → present perfect; yesterday, ago, in 2015 → past simple.

cards.answer: I have lived in Keren since 2018. Before that I lived in Mendefera for six years.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Every morning, my father ________ a cup of traditional coffee before he walks to his office.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The time-marker 'Every morning' indicates a habitual, repeated action in the present. This requires the Present Simple tense ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_{\text{1/s/es}}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often fail to match the verb to the singular subject 'my father' (3rd person singular), choosing the base form 'drink' (Option C). Option A ('is drinking') is continuous, which is incorrect for habitual actions.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Every morning' (ነፍሲ ወከፍ ንግሆ) ዝብል ናይ ግዜ መመልከቲ ልሙድ ተግባር (habitual action) ስለ ዝሕብር፡ እቲ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ኣብ Simple Present ክኸውን ኣለዎ። እቲ ዋና ባእታ 'my father' (ነጸላ) ስለ ዝኾነ ድማ እቲ ግሲ 's' ወሲዱ 'drinks' (Option B) ይኸውን።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Listen! The national choir ________ the anthem in the main hall right now.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The imperative 'Listen!' and 'right now' indicate an action in progress at the exact moment of speaking, requiring the Present Continuous tense ($$\text{S} + \text{am/is/are} + \text{V-ing}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students must identify 'The national choir' as a singular collective noun, which requires the singular auxiliary 'is'. Choosing 'are singing' (Option C) is a common agreement error.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Listen!' (ስምዕ!) ከምኡ ውን 'right now' (ሕጂ) ዝብሉ ቃላት እቲ ተግባር ኣብቲ ናይ ዕላል እዋን ይፍጸም ከም ዘሎ ስለ ዝሕብሩና፡ Present Continuous ክንጥቀም ኣለና። 'The national choir' (መዘምራን - ነጸላ እኩብ ስም) ስለ ዝኾነ ድማ ቅኑዕ መልሲ 'is singing' (Option B) እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Listen to those people, what language _________?
cards.why: The word 'Listen' indicates an action happening **now**. Therefore, we use the **Present Continuous** tense ('are they speaking').

tips.text: Revise The English Tense System with the quick checks and match game.

games.title: Match the tense to its use

pairs.b: finished actions at a past time
an action in progress in the past

questions.q: Every morning, my father ________ a cup of traditional coffee before he walks to his office.
questions.label: 1. Every morning, my father ________ a cup of traditional coffe
why: The time-marker 'Every morning' indicates a habitual, repeated action in the present. This requires the Present Simple tense ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_{\text{1/s/es}}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Listen! The national choir ________ the anthem in the main hall right now.
questions.label: 2. Listen! The national choir ________ the anthem in the main h
why: The imperative 'Listen!' and 'right now' indicate an action in progress at the exact moment of speaking, requiring the Present Continuous tense ($$\text{S} + \text{am/is/are} + \text{V-ing}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: I ________ the main reason for his sudden decision to leave the scholarship program.
questions.label: 3. I ________ the main reason for his sudden decision to leave
why: 'Understand' is a stative verb representing a cognitive state. Stative verbs cannot be used in continuous/progressive aspects ($$\times \text{be} + \text{V-ing}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: While we ________ for the school bus, it suddenly started to rain heavily.
questions.label: 4. While we ________ for the school bus, it suddenly started to
why: The conjunction 'While' is followed by the Past Continuous to show a long, ongoing past action. The subject is 'we' (plural), requiring the plural auxiliary 'were'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: The young candidate was presenting her research proposal when the power ________ down.
questions.label: 5. The young candidate was presenting her research proposal whe
why: The conjunction 'when' is followed by the Past Simple to introduce a sudden, completed action that interrupted an ongoing background action ($$\text{Past Continuous} + \text{when} + \text{Past Simple}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: While my brother was studying in his room, I ________ a historical novel in the living room.
questions.label: 6. While my brother was studying in his room, I ________ a hist
why: This sentence describes two parallel, ongoing actions happening at the same time in the past. Both clauses must use the Past Continuous tense ($$\text{Past Continuous} + \text{while} + \text{Past Continuous}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: The scientific fact is that the earth ________ around the sun in approximately 365 days.
questions.label: 7. The scientific fact is that the earth ________ around the su
why: The sentence states a scientific fact (general truth). General truths must strictly be expressed in the Present Simple tense ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_{\text{1/s/es}}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: The regional educational bureau ________ the newly constructed high school last month.
questions.label: 8. The regional educational bureau ________ the newly construct
why: The time-marker 'last month' specifies a definite completed time in the past. This strictly requires the Past Simple tense ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_2$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Currently, many citizens ________ that the economic reforms will stabilize the local market.
questions.label: 9. Currently, many citizens ________ that the economic reforms
why: 'Believe' is a stative verb of belief/opinion. Even though the time-marker 'Currently' suggests present progressive, stative verbs must remain in the Present Simple.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: At this time yesterday, we ________ the national mathematics matriculation examination.
questions.label: 10. At this time yesterday, we ________ the national mathematics
why: The time-marker 'At this time yesterday' specifies an exact, ongoing moment in the past. This requires the Past Continuous tense ($$\text{S} + \text{was/were} + \text{V-ing}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: My grandmother ____ coffee every afternoon.
questions.label: 11. My grandmother ____ coffee every afternoon.

similar.q: Complete: He ____ (go) to church on Sundays.
Complete: We ____ (eat) injera every day.

why: Habits use the present simple; singular subject → makes.
Present continuous is for actions happening now.
questions.tip: Present simple = habits and facts; present continuous = now or temporary; past simple = finished past; past continuous = action in progress in the past. Stative verbs (know, believe, own) are rarely continuous.

questions.q: Listen! Someone ____ at the door.
questions.label: 12. Listen! Someone ____ at the door.

similar.q: Complete: Look! It ____ (snow / rain).
Complete: Be quiet! The baby ____ (sleep).

why: "Listen!" shows the action is happening now.
questions.tip: Present simple = habits and facts; present continuous = now or temporary; past simple = finished past; past continuous = action in progress in the past. Stative verbs (know, believe, own) are rarely continuous.

questions.q: I ____ the answer now.
questions.label: 13. I ____ the answer now.

similar.q: Correct: I am believing you.
Correct: She is owning two cars.

why: "know" is a stative verb (a state, not an action).
Stative verbs are normally used in simple forms, even with "now".
So: I know the answer now.
questions.tip: Present simple = habits and facts; present continuous = now or temporary; past simple = finished past; past continuous = action in progress in the past. Stative verbs (know, believe, own) are rarely continuous.

questions.q: While we ____ for the bus, it started to rain.
questions.label: 14. While we ____ for the bus, it started to rain.

similar.q: Complete: While she ____ (cook), the phone rang.
Complete: I ____ (read) while my brother was sleeping.

why: "While" introduces a longer action in progress in the past.
The short action (started to rain) is past simple.
questions.tip: Present simple = habits and facts; present continuous = now or temporary; past simple = finished past; past continuous = action in progress in the past. Stative verbs (know, believe, own) are rarely continuous.

questions.q: Correct the error: "Yesterday I am going to the market."
questions.label: 15. Correct the error: "Yesterday I am going to the market."

similar.q: Correct: Last year she teaches in Keren.
similar.a: Last year she taught in Keren.

similar.q: Correct: Two days ago we are visiting Massawa.
similar.a: Two days ago we visited Massawa.

questions.answer: Yesterday I went to the market.
why: Present continuous refers to now or future plans.
questions.tip: Present simple = habits and facts; present continuous = now or temporary; past simple = finished past; past continuous = action in progress in the past. Stative verbs (know, believe, own) are rarely continuous.

questions.q: This week I ____ at my uncle's house because our house is being painted.
questions.label: 16. This week I ____ at my uncle's house because our house is being painted.

similar.q: Complete: She usually walks, but this week she ____ (take) the bus.
Complete: They ____ (live) with friends until the repairs finish.

why: "This week" and the reason show a temporary situation.
Temporary situations use the present continuous.
questions.tip: Present simple = habits and facts; present continuous = now or temporary; past simple = finished past; past continuous = action in progress in the past. Stative verbs (know, believe, own) are rarely continuous.

questions.q: Read: "Every morning Ruth wakes up at five and helps her mother. Today, however, she is sleeping late because she studied until midnight yesterday." Why is Ruth sleeping late today?
questions.label: 17. Read: "Every morning Ruth wakes up at five and helps her mother. Today, however, she is sleeping…

similar.q: Which tense shows Ruth's habit?
Which tense shows today's exception?

why: Answer A: She studied until midnight yesterday.
The because-clause gives the reason: "she studied until midnight yesterday".
"Every morning ... wakes up at five" shows her normal habit.
"Today ... is sleeping late" is a temporary exception.
questions.tip: Present simple = habits and facts; present continuous = now or temporary; past simple = finished past; past continuous = action in progress in the past. Stative verbs (know, believe, own) are rarely continuous.

questions.q: The train ____ at 6:30 tomorrow morning according to the timetable.
questions.label: 18. The train ____ at 6:30 tomorrow morning according to the timetable.

similar.q: Complete: The film ____ (start) at 8 tonight.
Complete: The shop ____ (open) at 9 tomorrow.

why: Timetables and schedules use the present simple even for the future.
So: The train leaves at 6:30 tomorrow.
This is a common exam trap.
questions.tip: Present simple = habits and facts; present continuous = now or temporary; past simple = finished past; past continuous = action in progress in the past. Stative verbs (know, believe, own) are rarely continuous.

questions.q: When I arrived, the guests ____ dinner, so I joined them.
questions.label: 19. When I arrived, the guests ____ dinner, so I joined them.

similar.q: Complete: When we came in, she ____ (play) the krar.
Complete: When the bell rang, the teacher ____ (write) on the board.

why: The meal was in progress when I arrived (I joined them).
Past simple "had" would suggest they ate after I arrived.
questions.tip: Present simple = habits and facts; present continuous = now or temporary; past simple = finished past; past continuous = action in progress in the past. Stative verbs (know, believe, own) are rarely continuous.

questions.q: True or false: "Water is boiling at 100 °C" is the best way to state a scientific fact.
questions.label: 20. True or false: "Water is boiling at 100 °C" is the best way to state a scientific fact.

similar.q: State as a fact: The sun (rise) in the east.
similar.a: The sun rises in the east.

similar.q: State as a fact: Plants (need) sunlight.

why: False. Scientific facts use the present simple.
The correct sentence is "Water boils at 100 °C".
Present continuous would describe one particular moment.
questions.tip: Present simple = habits and facts; present continuous = now or temporary; past simple = finished past; past continuous = action in progress in the past. Stative verbs (know, believe, own) are rarely continuous.
